content.text: {"steps":[{"id":"s1","description":"List and read the relevant project documents, especially candidate_specs.md and any documents describing lifetime, radiation, aging, optical stability, or operational constraints for radiator materials."},{"id":"s2","description":"From candidate_specs.md, extract the three allowed radiator candidates and their relevant properties; identify any candidates that fail the lifetime/performance-stability requirement and exclude them from further consideration."},{"id":"s3","description":"For each lifetime-qualified radiator candidate, run simulate_separation at representative thicknesses across the allowed 1–6 cm range, including at least 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, and 6 cm, and record the numeric pion/kaon separation results."},{"id":"s4","description":"Refine the scan around the best-performing thickness for each viable radiator, using additional simulate_separation runs at nearby thickness values within 1–6 cm as needed, and record all numeric results."},{"id":"s5","description":"Compare the maximum simulated pion/kaon separation achieved by each lifetime-qualified radiator and identify the single radiator and thickness with the best separation at 10 GeV/c for the final recommendation."}]}
